newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares end up sharply on bargain-hunting.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end up sharply on bargain-hunting.

text.p: Shenzhen's B shares on Monday defied worries over the suspension last Friday of several companies in the A share market and surged on bargain-hunting, analysts said.
The foreign currency B index closed at 166.85 points, up 7.79 or 4.89 percent, on turnover of HK$105.9 million against Friday's HK$122.7 million.
The domestic currency A index rose 5.07 points or 1.08 percent to 472.43 on turnover of 6.7 billion yuan, compared with 11.6 billion yuan on Friday.
"Some risk-takers jumped in to buy after seeing that Shenzhen Development Bank did not pull down the markets when it resumed trading in the afternoon," a broker at China Guotai Securities said.

Large-capitalisation Shenzhen Development Bank Co's A shares -- which were suspended in the morning after the bank announced it might have been involved in stock trading irregularities -- closed at 36.97 yuan, down just 0.17 yuan.
"The price (of Shenzhen Development Bank) did not plunge because the dividend plan remained intact," the Guotai broker said.

The bank said that although it was investigating possible stock trading irregularities in 1996, plans to make a five-for-10 bonus share issue and 0.2 yuan per share cash dividend based on 1996 profits were unchanged.

"But the small trading volume shows people are nervous after the indices slid last week, following the suspension of several stocks," an analyst at J&A Securities said. "We are going to see volatile trading ahead."
The suspension of A share companies Shenzhen Energy Investment Co Ltd and Luzhou Old Cellar Co Ltd on Friday for investigations into share price movements sent Shenzhen stocks down, analysts said.

Rumours that China may temporarily ban several major brokerages from carrying out securities trading on their own accounts as a punishment for irregularities also weighed on market sentiment, traders said.
Chinese securities officials have declined to comment.
In the B share market, Shenzhen Merchants Shekou Port Service Holdings Co Ltd was the top gainer, rising HK$0.47 or 9.94 percent to HK$5.20.
In the A share market, the two companies suspended on Friday, Luzhou Old Cellars and Shenzhen Energy, both plunged to their 10 percent limit-down to close at 28.53 yuan and 19.13 yuan respectively.
